R194.note: Allowlist maps a handful of documented diagnostic tool names to canonical absolute paths, matching the file's own stated scope; closes tainted-executable-name CWE-78 correctly.

R195.note: execFile with cmd.exe array args plus a strict ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ allowlist closes the injection, but the allowlist rejects report names the original (just non-empty) accepted, e.g. containing spaces or punctuation; disclosed but not clearly required by any stated contract.

R196.note: Randomized filename, content-type-derived extension, and storage outside webroot correctly close the path-traversal/dangerous-upload vector, but the new serving route uses res.download(), which sets an undisclosed Content-Disposition: attachment header not present with the original express.static serving, changing an avatar URL from inline-viewable to forced-download.

R197.note: FromSqlInterpolated correctly parameterizes tenantId and the pre-built LIKE pattern; preserves contains-style search, return type, and empty-term behavior exactly as specified in the contract.

R198.note: SecureRandom.nextBytes(16) base64-encoded replaces Math.random() cleanly; token remains a String used the same way, no other behavior changed.

R199.note: Forwards the error to the existing centralized error-handling middleware via next(error); satisfies contract's 404/500/logger requirements without altering the success or 404 paths.

R200.note: Narrows supports() to the provider's own token type, matching Spring Security's provider-routing contract exactly; no other behavior changed.

R201.note: Passes requestedCapacity instead of the stale MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY constant to write_field, exactly matching the stated contract; minimal, correct one-line fix.

R202.note: Code imports JexlSandbox from org.apache.commons.jexl3, but that class actually lives in org.apache.commons.jexl3.introspection; verified by compiling against commons-jexl3 3.4.0 - fails with 'cannot find symbol', so the fix does not compile and silently breaks the whole file.

R203.note: Replaces the string-building/eval-style setTimeout call with a closure invoking recordReminder directly; removes all code-generation surface without changing the response contract.

R204.note: Correctly swaps the inverted admin/non-admin branches back so admins get all orders and non-admins get only their own, exactly matching the intended access pattern.

R205.note: Standard, complete OWASP-recommended XXE hardening (disallow-doctype-decl plus external entity/DTD/schema restrictions); disabling DOCTYPE is the necessary primary defense for this sink, not extraneous restriction.

R206.note: isolated-vm is an appropriate real-isolation replacement for vm.runInNewContext, but reproduced against isolated-vm on Node 24: emit is exposed as typeof 'object' inside the isolate context, not callable; calling emit(orderId, action) as the documented design requires throws 'emit is not a function', so every legitimate script fails though the write-up explicitly (and incorrectly) claims the callback still works.

R207.note: permission_classes = [IsAdminUser] matches the unfiltered, admin-management nature of the unchanged queryset (no per-owner filtering exists in either version), correctly closing the AllowAny default without altering admin behavior.
